answer_text:
Let

\[
R=\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i \left(\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{125}\right)^{16}.
\]

We want the smallest \(C\) such that

\[
C\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{2005}\ge R
\]

for all positive \(x_1,\dots,x_5\).

---

### 1. Sharpness: equality at \(x_1=\cdots=x_5\)

Take \(x_1=\cdots=x_5=t>0\). Then

\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{2005}=5t^{2005}
\]

and

\[
\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i\left(\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{125}\right)^{16}
=t^5(5t^{125})^{16}
=5^{16}t^{2005}.
\]

Thus the inequality requires

\[
C\cdot 5t^{2005}\ge 5^{16}t^{2005},
\]

so

\[
C\ge 5^{15}.
\]

Therefore the smallest possible constant is at least \(5^{15}\).

---

### 2. Prove that \(C=5^{15}\) works

By the multinomial theorem,

\[
\left(\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{125}\right)^{16}
=
\sum_{\substack{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5=16\\ \alpha_i\ge 0}}
\frac{16!}{\alpha_1!\cdots \alpha_5!}
\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i^{125\alpha_i}.
\]

Multiplying by \(\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i\), we get

\[
R=
\sum_{\substack{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5=16\\ \alpha_i\ge 0}}
\frac{16!}{\alpha_1!\cdots \alpha_5!}
\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i^{125\alpha_i+1}.
\]

For a fixed multi-index \(\alpha\), set

\[
\beta_i=125\alpha_i+1.
\]

Then \(\beta_i>0\) and

\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 \beta_i
=125(16)+5
=2005.
\]

By weighted AM-GM,

\[
\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i^{\beta_i}
=
\prod_{i=1}^5 \left(x_i^{2005}\right)^{\beta_i/2005}
\le
\sum_{i=1}^5 \frac{\beta_i}{2005}x_i^{2005}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\prod_{i=1}^5 x_i^{125\alpha_i+1}
\le
\sum_{i=1}^5 \frac{125\alpha_i+1}{2005}x_i^{2005}.
\]

Substituting this into the expansion of \(R\),

\[
R\le
\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{2005}
\left[
\frac{1}{2005}
\sum_{\substack{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5=16\\ \alpha_i\ge 0}}
\frac{16!}{\alpha_1!\cdots \alpha_5!}
(125\alpha_i+1)
\right].
\]

Let the bracketed quantity for a fixed \(i\) be \(A_i\). By symmetry, \(A_1=\cdots=A_5\). Hence

\[
5A_i
=
\frac{1}{2005}
\sum_{\substack{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5=16\\ \alpha_i\ge 0}}
\frac{16!}{\alpha_1!\cdots \alpha_5!}
\sum_{i=1}^5 (125\alpha_i+1).
\]

But

\[
\sum_{i=1}^5 (125\alpha_i+1)
=125(\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5)+5
=125\cdot 16+5
=2005.
\]

Thus

\[
5A_i
=
\sum_{\substack{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5=16\\ \alpha_i\ge 0}}
\frac{16!}{\alpha_1!\cdots \alpha_5!}.
\]

By the multinomial theorem,

\[
\sum_{\substack{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_5=16\\ \alpha_i\ge 0}}
\frac{16!}{\alpha_1!\cdots \alpha_5!}
=
(1+1+1+1+1)^{16}
=
5^{16}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
5A_i=5^{16},
\]

so

\[
A_i=5^{15}.
\]

Hence

\[
R\le 5^{15}\sum_{i=1}^5 x_i^{2005}.
\]

So \(C=5^{15}\) indeed works.

---

Since \(C=5^{15}\) works and no smaller constant can work, the smallest possible constant is

\[
\boxed{5^{15}}.
\]
